# Deploybot

> Deploybot lets any AI agent that speaks MCP run your own servers, without handing it SSH keys or a cloud token. It can only deploy what your catalog allows, as you, after a confirm step. People use the same controls through a web console.

Deploybot is a control plane for your own hosts: Raspberry Pis, VPSs and cloud VMs. A small agent, bot-agent, runs on each host and dials out to the Deploybot API, so hosts open no inbound ports and can sit behind NAT. Project owners keep a catalog of approved container images and programs. People and AI agents can deploy, run, stop, restart and roll back only those entries, within their role in the project.

Website: https://deploybot.dev/

Hosted service: console at https://console.deploybot.dev, MCP server at https://mcp.deploybot.dev/mcp. Sign-in is with Google. The source is public on GitHub, and you can self-host it.

## How the safety model works

- An MCP client acts as the signed-in user, with that user's role in each project, and no more.
- Only catalog entries can run. There are no free-form commands, no shell tool and no file tools.
- Every change made over MCP (deploy, rollback, run, stop, restart, health-check and catalog edits) first returns a plan and a `confirmation_id`. Nothing happens until the `confirm` tool is called with the same `idempotency_key`.
- Each host has its own root-owned allowlist of images and projects that the server cannot change.
- Secret values (env sets, files and registry logins) are encrypted at rest and write-only for people. MCP tools return env key names, never env values. Logs are redacted.
- Changes are recorded in an audit log.

## Instructions for AI agents

- Read before you change: call `list_catalog`, `entry_status` or `get_health_checks` first.
- Show the user the plan that a change returns, and call `confirm` only after the user agrees. Use the same `idempotency_key` as the call that returned the plan.
- Do not put secret values in `spec.env` on catalog entries. Secrets belong in env sets entered in the web console.
- A `forbidden` or `not_found` result means the user's role does not allow the call or cannot see the resource. Do not retry it with other ids.

## Connect an MCP client

- [bot-mcp-server README](https://github.com/more-than-code/bot-mcp-server/blob/main/README.md): the full tool reference, the OAuth sign-in, and `deploybot login` for clients without a browser.
- Claude Code example: `claude mcp add --transport http deploybot https://mcp.deploybot.dev/mcp`. Any client with Streamable HTTP and OAuth can connect the same way; it discovers sign-in from `https://mcp.deploybot.dev/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`.

## MCP tools

- Read: `list_projects`, `list_hosts`, `list_services`, `list_processes`, `query_metrics`, `service_health_history`, `get_health_checks`, `list_catalog`.
- Contact a host live (read only): `host_snapshot`, `probe_service`, `entry_status`, `entry_logs`.
- Change, with plan and confirm: `deploy_entry`, `rollback_entry`, `run_entry`, `stop_entry`, `restart_entry`, `set_health_checks`, `create_catalog_entry`, `update_catalog_entry`, `delete_catalog_entry`.
- `confirm`: carries out a plan after the user agrees.

## Add a host

- AI agents: follow "Enrol with an AI agent" in the install guide below. The user gives you access to the host (their SSH, a shell on the host, their cloud console, or commands they paste); you run the download, checks and install with the policy flags they agree to, then hand them the enrol command from the install output. The user creates the join token in the console, which gives them instructions for you that include the server URL; put exactly that URL into the enrol command, never a guessed one. The user types the token at the enrol prompt themselves. Never ask for, read or handle the join token.
- [Install bot-agent](https://github.com/more-than-code/bot-agent/blob/main/docs/install.md): `install.sh`, enrolling with a one-time join token, the optional root runner for catalog entries, and the host allowlist (`/etc/bot-agent/runner.toml`).
- [bot-agent README](https://github.com/more-than-code/bot-agent/blob/main/README.md): what the agent collects, how it deploys images and programs, and health checks.

## Features

- Resilience: deploys wait for health (Docker health status or HTTP/TCP checks); an unhealthy deploy rolls back to the previous container automatically; one-step rollback to an earlier image digest; a health failure policy per service; programs run as systemd units and survive reboot.
- Visibility: host metrics with history, running processes and discovered services, health check history per service, container logs with secrets redacted, container logs capped at 10 MB × 3 by default.
- Teams: owner, admin and viewer roles per project, invite links that expire (single-use by default), per-entry rights to run, stop, restart or deploy for a role or a user, a host shared with other projects at metrics or deploy level, and one-time join tokens for adding hosts.

## Self-hosting from source

- [bot-api-server](https://github.com/more-than-code/bot-api-server/blob/main/README.md): the API, the only part that writes the Postgres database and decides permissions. AGPL-3.0-only.
- [bot-mcp-server](https://github.com/more-than-code/bot-mcp-server/blob/main/README.md): the stateless MCP gateway. AGPL-3.0-only.
- [bot-console](https://github.com/more-than-code/bot-console/blob/main/README.md): the SvelteKit web console. AGPL-3.0-only.
- [bot-agent](https://github.com/more-than-code/bot-agent/blob/main/README.md): the host agent, in Go. Apache-2.0.

## Optional

- [API contract](https://github.com/more-than-code/bot-api-server/blob/main/docs/contracts/api-v1.md): every `/v1` endpoint, request and response.
- [OAuth contract](https://github.com/more-than-code/bot-api-server/blob/main/docs/contracts/oauth-v1.md): sign-in for the console, the CLI and MCP clients.
- [Agent protocol](https://github.com/more-than-code/bot-agent/blob/main/docs/contracts/agent-protocol-v1.md): the messages between bot-agent and the API.
- [API design](https://github.com/more-than-code/bot-api-server/blob/main/docs/design.md): how the API server is built.
